messages:
anya: Heads-up — we saw a sharp GPU saturation event in us-west-2 around 09:12. Queue depth jumped from ~40 -> 600 in 3m, p95 latency spiked and admission started returning 503s.
raj: saw it too. looks correlated with a marketing push + low headroom on the cluster. current autoscaler配置 has min_nodes=10, max_nodes=120, scale_down_delay=300s.
sophie: is this the same cluster that has the small-region packing? we had fewer spare slots per AZ there.
anya: yep, that cluster is packed for cost. we collapsed headroom to ~3% to save $$ — clearly too aggressive for bursty traffic.
mike: quick data: prom query for queue depth: `sum(kube_pod_container_resource_requests{resource="gpu"})` nah wait, better: `sum(inference_queue_depth{cluster="us-west-2"}) by (pool)` — p95 around 520 at peak.
raj: idea: add a headroom reservoir + admission backpressure ramp that triggers at 60% GPU utilization instead of 80%. So we smooth the admit rate earlier.
sophie: agree. we should also smooth the autoscaler step size and increase preprovision buffer for that pool. current preprovision_threshold was 0.02 (2%), bump to 0.12 (12%).
anya: propose short term hotfix: 1) raise headroom target to 15% for us-west-2 pool, 2) reduce scale_in aggressiveness (scale_down_delay=900s), 3) enable admission token-bucket with burst=30 and rate=per-gpu * 0.6.
julia: can we patch admission config via a feature flag so we can rollback quickly?
raj: yes, we have `feature.flags.admission.dynamic_headroom` — I'll roll a canary to 5% of traffic first.
mike: config snippet I'm thinking:
```
admission:
  mode: token_bucket
  token_burst: 30
  per_gpu_rate: 60 # tokens/sec per GPU slot
  headroom_target: 0.15
  smoothing_window: 30s
autoscaler:
  scale_down_delay: 900s
  preprovision_threshold: 0.12
  max_step: 0.25
```
anya: looks good. also add a metric alert on sustained queue_depth > 200 for 5m to auto-mute canary if it oscillates.
raj: I'll kick off the change on staging and a canary in production to 5% (flagged). plan: 10m staging smoke, then 30m canary, then 2h ramp if stable.
sophie: please add a PromQL dashboard panel for "admit_rate / capacity" and the new headroom metric.
julia: tagging on-call: @mike — can you be ready for rollback if the canary misbehaves?
mike: on it. will monitor p95 latency, queue_depth, and instance provisioning lag. also watch cost delta metric — we should understand $$ impact of added headroom.
infra-bot: deployment started: feature.flags.admission.dynamic_headroom -> canary (5%) by raj at 09:45 UTC. runbook: https://redwood.internal/runbooks/infra/admission-backpressure
anya: reminder: keep logging minimal for canary to not flood our ELK. only increase verbosity if we hit unexpected errors.
raj: staging smoke passed. canary looks healthy for 20m; queue depth in canary pool peaked at 80 vs 320 previously, admit rejections dropped by ~70%.
sophie: promising. any latency regressions?
mike: p95 latency down 18% in canary slice. provisioning lag up slightly (+12s avg) but acceptable.
julia: schedule: continue 2h ramp. postmortem if we need to revert.
raj: rolling to 25% now. will post updates every 30m.
anya: action items: - raj: rollout and monitor canary - mike: ready for rollback and cost snapshot - sophie: update dashboards - julia: sign off on SLA impact
infra-bot: canary at 25% successful. next step: 100% ramp in 2h unless alarms fire.
anya: thanks team. follow-up: we should build an autoscaler test harness that replays marketing-style bursts so we don't tune blind. ticketed in backlog. :spiral_notepad:
raj: filed INFRA-1128 with load script and replay data.
mike: noted for next oncall rotation.
infra-bot: deployment complete: feature.flags.admission.dynamic_headroom -> 100% at 11:32 UTC.
anya: closing notes: net effect — fewer 503s, lower p95, added ~8% steady-state cost for extra headroom. looks like a good tradeoff for now. we can optimize quantization and batching later to reduce running cost. :thumbsup:
